What I grew up we had 3 tv channels, no vcr or anything else. The question what do I want to watch was a pretty easy one. Just pick the best out of 3.

This was the case for many things, where are we going on holiday was pretty much, which one of the 3 neighbor country's are we going to. And for us it was always what part of France (my parents spoke French and almost no German).

So anyway back to today. We have multiple streaming services with hundreds or even thousands of different movies and TV shows. More channels than you even remember all the names. We can travel to pretty much any place on the planet, and you don't need to be a millionaire to do it.

I am still not really sure if we are blessed with all this choice or cursed?

There is no freedom of choice, there is only an illusion. For example you can not choose not to die or breathe etc.

More choice is almost always good. I think with the level of choice we have nowadays it's more important to make informed decisions & to learn how to process all this information being bombarded at us, ie critical thinking is a good place to start because it's a foundation on how to separate bullshit from truth.

Choice implies that somebody is offering you options and you pick one of them. This is dangerous.

As long as you limit yourself to choices offered by others you set yourself in a prison. The illusion of choice - You can have a normal Coke or you can have a Diet Coke - the person offering you that choice conveniently omits to mention that you have other choices.

So having a choice is about being aware of all the options, especially the ones which are not mentioned.

There's the notion of the 'paradox of choice' - if you give people too many choices, it overwhelms them, whereas if you only give them a couple they find it easy to choose. That said, I enjoy being able to watch whatever I want whenever I want.

Freedom is not necessarily a good thing. What is done with freedom makes it good or bad. Personal responsibility is what makes those who use freedom to its greatest advantages to be truly successful. That is not saying that people can not successfully abuse freedom as well. But what freedom is, of necessity due to abuse, is the only rational course. Someone is always on top, no matter what system is in place. Freedom, or liberty, is simply the only way to "level the playing field".
